results.previous_best: $\widetilde{O}(n^\omega \log(\Delta)/\varepsilon)$ time with $O(\mathsf{OPT}_{2\alpha(1+\varepsilon)}\log n)$ edges (Khanna, Padaki, Waingarten, SODA 2026); $O(n^{2.5})$ time with $O(\mathsf{OPT}_\alpha\log n)$ edges
results.quote: Theorem 1.2. For any \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a randomized algorithm that, given point set P, arbitrary distance function \(d(\cdot,\cdot)\), and \(\alpha>1\), constructs an \(\alpha\)-navigable graph, with at most \(O\big(OPT_{\alpha(1+\varepsilon)}logn\big)\) edges, where \(OPT_{\alpha(1+\varepsilon)}\) is the size of the sparsest \(\alpha(1+\varepsilon)\)-navigable graph. The algorithm runs in \(\widetilde{O}\big(n^\omega\cdot log(\Delta_P)/\varepsilon\big)\) time, where \(\Delta_P\) is the set’s aspect ratio.

Corollary 3.12. Let P be a set of n points with aspect ratio \(\Delta_P\), after normalizing its minimum nonzero pairwise distance to 1. For every \(\tau\ge 0\) and \(0<\epsilon\le 1\), there is a randomized algorithm running in \(\widetilde{O}\left(n^\omega\frac{\Delta_P}{\epsilon}\right)\) time that constructs a \(\tau\)-monotonic graph G such that, with high probability, every \(s\in P\) has out-degree at most \(O(\mathsf{OPT}_{\tau+\epsilon}(s)logn)\), where \(\mathsf{OPT}_{\tau+\epsilon}(s)\) is the minimum out-degree required at s in any \((\tau+\epsilon)\)-monotonic graph. Consequently, \(|E|\le O(logn)\cdot\mathsf{OPT}_{\tau+\epsilon}\).

results.bound: No $O(n^{2.5-\delta})$ algorithm for any constant $\delta>0$ unless the APSP conjecture is falsified
results.quote: Corollary 4.9. For every constant \(\varepsilon>0\), there does not exist an \(O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon})\) algorithm for \(\alpha\)-navigability testing unless the APSP conjecture is falsified.
